# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

Stopping immediately — no further tool calls, no more sub-agent dispatch, nothing reverted or fixed on my end. Here is the honest state of the investigation at the point of stopping.

## Critical finding — this overrides everything else in this report

**A concurrent process was actively rewriting the exact file under test, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`, during this test session.** This is CONFIRMED, not speculation, from three independent sources:

1. **Two of my three sub-agents independently observed it**, with matching specifics: the file's content cycled through multiple distinct states within minutes — at one point the entire C1 feature (`resolveRepresentativeColour`, `selectColourScopedImages`) was gone, reverted to the old pre-fix "biggest group anywhere" logic; later it reappeared reworked with renamed identifiers (`selectColourScopedImages`→`selectScopedImages`, `COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`→`COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`) and new docblock text. Both sub-agents independently ran SHA-256/diff checks proving *their own* temporary test edits were cleanly reverted before this churn started — they each ruled themselves out as the cause.
2. One sub-agent found a live `claude bg-spare` daemon (PID 57882, ~19+ minutes CPU time) running against this same working tree via `ps aux` — a separate session actively operating on this branch concurrently.
3. **I observed it myself, first-party**, not just via relay: my own two `git diff --stat` checks on the same two files, taken minutes apart while otherwise idle, disagree — first `224/237` lines changed per file (`421` insertions total), then `205/254` (`419` insertions total). I did not touch these files between those checks. That's independent confirmation the target was moving under me too.

Both sub-agents correctly declined to run `git checkout --` on the file to "clean up," since — with zero staged changes and the whole uncommitted feature sitting only in the working tree — that command would have destroyed real, in-flight work (theirs or the other session's), not just a test artifact. I concur with that judgment call; I have not run any destructive command either.

**Practical consequence: no verdict in this report can be trusted as describing the file's current on-disk state.** Everything below reflects a specific snapshot captured before the churn was noticed, cross-checked internally for consistency at the time, but not guaranteed to match what's on disk right now.

## What was confirmed before the collision (snapshot-scoped, real execution, not speculation)

**Baseline gates (my own run, clean tree, before any dispatch):** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (exit 0). `npm run test`: 76 files / 1170 tests passed, including `productListCardMapper.test.ts` (29/29) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6). `npm run lint`: 63 problems (14 errors/49 warnings) — exact match to stated baseline, none in the two files under test. `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: 3 unacknowledged findings, exact match to baseline, none in these two files (the script doesn't even scan `pages/`).

**Colour-resolution edge cases (sub-agent 1, all CONFIRMED by real execution):**
- Stale/typo `representedProduct.id` matching no variant: already tested (`productListCardMapper.test.ts:208-211`), passes, safe.
- `variants: []` vs `variants: undefined`: not distinctly tested, but confirmed functionally identical code path (`[].find()` behaves exactly like `undefined?.find()`) — not a real gap.
- **🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF**: two variants sharing the same `productId` (malformed/duplicate data) — `.find()` silently returns the first array entry with no test, comment, or dev-time signal documenting "first wins" as the intended contract.
- **🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF**: `filterImageGroups` (real base-SFCC source, read directly) does a strict `===` compare with zero case-normalization. A casing mismatch between a variant's `variationValues.color` and the same hit's `imageGroups[].variationAttributes[].values[].value` was proven end-to-end to silently empty the entire gallery/hoverImage/primaryImageFallbacks (not "wrong colour" but total blackout) while `primaryImage` still renders fine. No test covers this today. Realism against actual SFCC data is unconfirmed either way — flagging as a real, untested gap, not a confirmed live defect.

**Mutation testing, viewType axis (sub-agent 2, CONFIRMED by real execution):** breaking only `viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE` → `'large'` (colour logic untouched) real-failed exactly 4 tests via `npx vitest run`, independently of the implementer's own "revert everything" mutation. **Colour axis (Mutation B) and a third blind-spot mutation (Mutation C) were never run** — the sub-agent halted when it detected the concurrent rewrite rather than produce unattributable results against a moving target. This is a real, unfilled gap in my falsification coverage, not a clean result.

**hoverImage/hit.image/conventions (sub-agent 3, CONFIRMED, captured before the cascade):**
- `selectColourScopedImages` runs twice per `selectProductListCard` call (proved via a real `console.count`, output `1` then `2`), once via `selectGalleryImages` and once directly for `hoverImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`. Confirmed pure/stateless, so this cannot cause the two to disagree — real, but a redundant-computation cost, not a correctness bug. ONE-OFF.
- `git diff 6d4fe0a` confirms `toCardImage` and the `primaryImage`/`return null` lines appear only as unchanged context — zero behavioural change to primary-image resolution, as the AC requires.
- **🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM**: `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'` is now independently typed in three files (`recentlyViewedCard.ts:83`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:108`, `productListCardMapper.ts:38`), each just commented to "match" the others, despite three existing shared-constant precedents in this codebase (`zimmProductCardShared.ts`, `footerShared.ts`, `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`). `COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` is confirmed NOT duplicated elsewhere — net-new, not a DRY violation on its own.
- SDK field names (`variant.productId`, `variant.variationValues`, `ProductRef.id`) confirmed real and correctly cased against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s actual `.d.ts`. The `as ShopperSearchTypes.ImageGroup[]` cast target is confirmed namespace-correct for `ProductSearchHit` specifically (more precise than a naive copy of the sibling files' own cast would have been), though still sitting on an implicit-`any` import with no comment at the cast site itself — same pre-existing, uncommented pattern as the two sibling files, not a new or worse instance.
- 🔵 note, PLAUSIBLE: `colourScopedImages.slice(2)`'s literal `2` isn't covered by the `{0,1,-1}` magic-number exception and has no named constant, unlike `[1]`/`[0]`.

## What I could not verify

- Whether the mutation-based falsification of the **colour axis specifically** (as opposed to viewType) holds up against an independently-chosen mutation — Mutation B/C were never completed.
- Part 4's conventions write-up from sub-agent 3 was gathered but explicitly flagged as not fully finished before it stopped.
- Whether the file's *current* on-disk content still matches anything analyzed above — explicitly not verifiable right now given the active external churn.
- Whether the pass criteria are met by whatever is on disk **at this moment** — I have not re-read the file since the churn was first reported, per the stop instruction.

Before this step gets a verdict from anyone, whoever owns the other active session (PID 57882 / `bg-spare`) needs to either finish and settle, or be paused, so the file stops changing under test.
